hero.eyebrow: Ethereum · Real Solidity, compiled and checked
hero.title: Ethereum & Smart Contracts: read it, reason about it, then build
hero.subtitle: Learn the account model and gas, read real Solidity line by line, tell reads from writes, spot the reentrancy trap and write a specification and test plan. Code examples were compiled and checked; you try them in the free Remix editor.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can read small smart contracts, explain what they cost and what can go wrong, and plan a safe deployment.

faq.q: Does the course run my code?
faq.a: No. Labs check your analysis and writing. You run the Solidity examples yourself in Remix, a free tool that works in your browser.
No. Remix has a built-in test environment, and test networks give free worthless ETH from faucets.

faq.q: Will this make me an auditor?
faq.a: No. It gives the foundation. The security and advanced Solidity courses in the series go further, and real audits need experienced professionals.

activities.title: Wei, gwei and ether
activities.objective: Convert between Ethereum's units, which are all powers of ten.
activities.scenario: Contracts count in wei, the smallest unit, because they cannot use decimals. 1 gwei is 1,000,000,000 wei and 1 ETH is 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 (10^18) wei.
steps: In C2 convert each amount in ETH (B) to wei: ETH times 10^18 using POWER(10,18).
In D2 convert wei to gwei: wei divided by 10^9.
Fill down rows 2 to 5.
In B8 work out how many wei are in 0.025 ETH using the same method (type the formula).

checks.label: C2 is one ether in wei
D3 is the tip in gwei
checks.hint: =C3/POWER(10,9)

checks.label: C5 is the smallest fee in wei
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B8 is 0.025 ETH in wei

activities.title: Work out an EIP-1559 fee
activities.objective: Calculate the total fee, the burned part and the tip from gas used, base fee and priority fee.
activities.scenario: Since the London upgrade (2021) each block has a base fee per unit of gas, set by the protocol and burned. A user adds a priority fee (a tip) for the block producer. The total price per gas is the base fee plus the tip, provided it does not exceed the user's maximum. (Teaching numbers; 1 ETH = 10^9 gwei.)
steps: In B8 work out the price per gas: base fee plus tip.
In B9 check the user's maximum fee per gas covers it: show OK if B3 is at least B8, otherwise Too low.
In B10 work out the total fee in gwei: gas used times price per gas.
In B11 work out the burned part in gwei: gas used times the base fee.
In B12 work out the tip paid to the producer in gwei: gas used times the tip.
In B13 convert the total fee to ETH: gwei divided by 1,000,000,000.
In B14 convert to rupees using the ETH price in B6.

checks.label: B8 is the price per gas
B9 is OK
checks.hint: =IF(B3>=B8,"OK","Too low")
checks.explain: The user's cap must cover the price.

checks.label: B10 is the total fee in gwei
B11 is the burned part
B12 is the tip
B13 is the total in ETH
B14 is the total in rupees

cells.A3: Maximum fee per gas the user allows (gwei)

activities.title: Budget the gas for a small project
activities.objective: Estimate what deploying and using a contract costs, so you can plan a testnet or live budget.
activities.scenario: Different actions use different amounts of gas. At a given gas price, work out the cost of each action and of a whole month of use. (Teaching numbers.)
steps: In D2 work out the cost of one action in ETH: gas used times gas price in gwei, divided by 1,000,000,000. Fill down to D5.
In E2 work out the monthly cost: the cost of one action times the number of times per month (C). Fill down.
In E7 total the monthly cost.
In E8 convert it to rupees using the ETH price in B9.
In B10 show Over budget if the monthly rupee cost is more than the budget in B11, else Within budget.

checks.label: D2 is the cost of deploying
checks.explain: Gas times price over a billion.

checks.label: E3 is the monthly cost of tips
E7 is the total in ETH
checks.hint: =SUM(E2:E5)

checks.label: E8 is the total in rupees
B12 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(E8>B11,"Over budget","Within budget")

activities.objective: Write a professional specification and test plan for a small contract, covering functions, access control, events, tests and risks.
activities.scenario: Use the TipJar contract as a model: people can send tips, the owner can withdraw. Specify an improved version that also lets the owner set a minimum tip and pause tipping. Write the spec and test plan.

Under Functions list at least five functions in bullets.
Under Test plan write a numbered list of at least six tests including a failing case.
Under Risks list at least three risks.
Keep it between 230 and 460 words.
